findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a Certified FOOD Protection Manager (CFPM) who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

On arrival there was not a CFPM available on site while foods were being handled and prepared. The facility manager (who had a CFPM) arrived during the inspection to correct the immediate violation. A hand out was given to them with the known current available CFPM courses. Ensure that there is a CFPM available at all times that foods are being prepared in the facility.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

On arrival the PIC was unable to provide proof that staff was notified in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report reportable symptoms and diagnosis. A fresh copy will be sent to the PIC via email later the same as the inspection. The PIC was instructed to have signed copies available prior to the scheduled follow-up.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.citation_text:
3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor. 

Cases of paper bowls were observed on the floor behind the door in the kitchen. The PIC was shown and instructed to stored all food contact surfaces off of the floor moving forward. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are stored off of the floor at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

The new shelf in the kitchen was observed to have exposed particle board on the edges. The PIC was shown and instructed to seal prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

The corner wall next to the refrigerators is observed with the corner cover and Nudo board pulling away at the bottom. The PIC is instructed to repair/reseal prior to the next routine inspection. Ensure that the facilities are maintained in good repair at all times to prevent possible contaminants and pest issues.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

No CFPM certificates were available during this inspection. PIC indicated that the main facility manager has taken the course but not the test. They appeared to be under the impression that only one person could have the certificate. Inspector discussed this and instructed them to have multiple CFPMs available so that all shifts could be covered by a CFPM.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. 

On arrival the staff was unaware of any written procedures related to cleaning up and disinfecting vomit/diarrheal events in the food facilities. Education was conducted and a copy of the Norovirus clean up procedures distributed by SCDPH was given during this inspection to correct the violation.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

No CFPM certificates were available during this inspection. PIC indicated that the kitchen manager has the certification but could not show it at this time. Ensure copies of the food certifications are available at the facility at all times.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. 

On arrival there was not a ready for use sanitizer available at the facility. Education was conducted and a bucket made during this inspection to correct.
